Latent triadic closure stochastic block model

latent_closure_block_state.Rd

Native C++ implementation of Peixoto's (2022) joint stochastic block model with \(L \ge 1\) generations of zero-inflated triadic closures, matching graph-tool's LatentClosureBlockState. Disentangles observed edges into homophily/community substrate edges versus triadic-closure edges and estimates per-vertex open/closed triad counts and transitivity.

Usage

latent_closure_block_state(graph, L = 1L, nested = TRUE,
  blocks = NULL, gen = NULL, w0 = NULL, loops = NULL, ex = NULL,
  degree_corrected = TRUE,
  degree_prior = c("distributed", "uniform"), q_max = Inf)

closure_description_length(state, breakdown = FALSE)

infer_triadic_closure(state, nsamples = 200L, burnin = 100L, thin = 1L,
  beta = 1, pedges = 0.5, c = 1, d = 0.01,
  sample_loops = TRUE, init_sbm = TRUE,
  collect_partitions = FALSE)

Arguments

graph

An undirected simple graph created by graph_create (no self-loops or parallel edges).

L

Maximum number of triadic closure generations (\(L \ge 1\)).

nested

Whether to use a nested (TRUE) or flat (FALSE) SBM substrate prior.

blocks

Optional initial substrate partition or hierarchy.

gen

Optional integer vector of length graph_num_edges(graph) in 0..L giving each edge's initial generation (0 = substrate, 1..L = triadic closure generation). Defaults to all 0L.

w0

Optional initial substrate edge multiplicities for generation-0 edges.

loops

Optional length-\(N\) integer vector of initial substrate self-loop multiplicities.

ex

Optional list of length graph_num_edges(graph) giving the 1-based closing ego vertex IDs for each closure edge (empty integer vectors for substrate edges).

degree_corrected

Whether the substrate SBM is degree-corrected.

degree_prior

Degree sequence hyperprior ("distributed" or "uniform").

q_max

Maximum degree cached in the partition-count table.

state

A rgraphtool_latent_closure_block_state object.

breakdown

If TRUE, return a named list with total, sbm, closure, per-generation layer_entropies, and per-vertex open/closed triad counts M and E.

nsamples, burnin, thin

Posterior MCMC sample count, burn-in sweeps, and thinning interval.

beta

Inverse MCMC temperature.

pedges

Probability of performing an edge-layer/ego sweep versus a substrate SBM partition sweep.

c, d

Substrate SBM proposal parameters.

sample_loops

Whether to sample latent substrate self-loop multiplicities during edge sweeps.

init_sbm

If TRUE and state starts from a single-group partition, initialize the substrate SBM partition before MCMC.

collect_partitions

If TRUE, return sampled substrate SBM partitions in partitions.

Value

latent_closure_block_state() returns a rgraphtool_latent_closure_block_state. closure_description_length() returns the exact joint description length (or a detailed breakdown list). infer_triadic_closure() returns a rgraphtool_closure_inference containing per-edge posterior layer probabilities (edges: substrate_prob, closure_prob, and gen_0..gen_L), per-generation vertex statistics (vertex_stats: average closed triads t, open triads m, and transitivity fraction c), the final state, and entropy trace.

References

Peixoto, T. P. (2022). Disentangling homophily, community structure, and triadic closure in networks. Physical Review X 12, 011004. doi:10.1103/PhysRevX.12.011004

See also

measured_block_state, predict_edges, demo("triadic_closure")

Examples

g <- graph_create(6, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(cbind(1:5, 2:6), c(6L, 1L), c(1L, 3L), c(3L, 5L)))
st <- latent_closure_block_state(g, L = 1L, nested = FALSE)
set.seed(1)
res <- infer_triadic_closure(st, nsamples = 40L, burnin = 30L, init_sbm = FALSE)
res$edges
#>   from to substrate_prob closure_prob gen_0 gen_1
#> 1    1  2          0.900        0.100 0.900 0.100
#> 2    1  3          0.900        0.100 0.900 0.100
#> 3    2  3          1.000        0.000 1.000 0.000
#> 4    3  4          1.000        0.000 1.000 0.000
#> 5    3  5          0.875        0.125 0.875 0.125
#> 6    4  5          1.000        0.000 1.000 0.000
#> 7    5  6          1.000        0.000 1.000 0.000
#> 8    1  6          1.000        0.000 1.000 0.000
